title: Correction to my SH no-fission negative: spot molecules do break up persistently (28 events in t=150-1000, both pieces >= 2 spots and still apart 50 t later), mostly early while the resource is depleted; it is fragmentation, not shown to be growth-then-fission
summary: My negative 20261026T0841-c37-sh-no-fission-negative said molecules 'never split'. It counted only net molecule numbers, which fall by coalescence. Tracking break-ups directly (fission.py, the setting ar=0.02 of scan_i, seed 0, census every 5 t) finds 99 break-ups of molecules with >= 2 spots. In 61 both pieces have >= 2 spots; 28 of 59 checkable events stay apart 50 t later (fission_ar02.txt). Examples: 31 spots -> 23 + 6 at t=170, 22 -> 20 + 18 at t=195, 30 -> 26 + 15 at t=215. The pieces don't sum to the parent because spots join and die within the 5 t census step. The crops (fission_events.png) show loose clusters tearing apart during the early die-back phase (the first 15 persistent events fall at t=170-355), not a molecule that grows on food and then divides. So D is open in this class: fission exists, but whether it is reproduction (growth, then a split into similar parts) is untested. The coalescence half of the negative still holds: net molecule counts fall in every setting.

finding.operator: Swift-Hohenberg spots + slow inhibitor + consumed resource
finding.control: persistence check: pieces in different molecules 50 t after the break
finding.result: 28 persistent break-ups (both pieces >= 2 spots) in t=150-1000 on seed 0; first 15 at t=170-355; coalescence still dominates the net count
